headline: Clemens tops group and calls new Grand Slam format tough
standfirst: Gabriel Clemens reached the last 16 for the first time since his 2019 debut but says the 48-player format favours fans over players.
body: Gabriel Clemens reached the last 16 of the Grand Slam of Darts for only the second time by beating Rusty-Jake Rodriguez 5-3 on Tuesday evening, taking top spot in his group. It is his first knockout appearance since his debut in 2019.

The German was under pressure late on. He missed chances to move 5-2 ahead, which kept Rodriguez alive; one more leg for the Austrian would have sent him through instead. Rodriguez missed a dart at double 19 to do so, and both men finished with a checkout rate below 25 per cent. "It was really nervous," Clemens said afterwards, calling himself the lucky man.

He and Luke Littler were the only players to reach the last 16 with just one group win. Clemens knew he needed to win 5-3 to be safe, as a defeat or a 5-4 win after Rodriguez took a fourth leg would have ended his tournament.
Clemens qualified by winning his first PDC title at Players Championship 24 this year. He had lost six finals on the tour before that, and he sealed the seventh with a 170 checkout.

On the new group format, he was blunt. "For the players, it's tough," he said, noting that every group match feels like a last-chance game. "For the people, it's great. I think for the players, before was better!"

The group stage criticism has come from several players this week. Clemens now faces Nathan Aspinall in the last 16 on Thursday. In 2019 he missed a match dart against Glen Durrant at this stage and lost 10-9.
